instruction: Add the Apple Human Interface Guidelines searching page (https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/searching) to your bookmarks bar.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to Apple HIG searching page, scrolled to understand content structure, opened terminal, used curl to download HTML, installed python-docx and beautifulsoup4, wrote a Python script to extract content between 'Searching' and 'Resources' sections, created notes.docx on Desktop. File was created (36KB) but content/formatting did not match the gold standard docx.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome to specific URLs, scroll web pages, open terminal, use curl to download files, install pip packages, write and execute Python scripts, create files on Desktop
metadata.failure_analysis: Model successfully created a docx file but the content extraction via regex and plain-text formatting did not match the gold standard document. The compare_docx_files evaluator found the documents too different despite fuzzy matching.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests navigation + bookmarking, which is simpler than the original content extraction task. Model demonstrated URL navigation capability; adding a bookmark is a natural next step within demonstrated skills.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to the Apple HIG searching page and bookmarking it. Evaluator checks bookmarks bar contains the expected URL using is_expected_bookmarks.

scoring_breakdown.bookmark: 1.0 - Bookmarks bar contains the Apple HIG searching URL

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads Chrome bookmarks from the Bookmarks JSON file and returns the roots object containing bookmark_bar
Metric is_expected_bookmarks correctly handles the bookmark_bar_websites_urls type, extracting URLs from bookmark_bar children
Expected URL exactly matches the URL specified in the instruction
Data flow is correct: get_bookmarks() -> roots dict -> is_expected_bookmarks checks bookmark_bar children URLs against expected URLs

Minor concern: metric uses set equality (==) rather than subset check, so pre-existing bookmarks on the bar would cause a false negative. However, the 'chrome' snapshot likely starts with a clean bookmark bar, making this acceptable.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using issubset() instead of set equality to be robust against pre-existing bookmarks on the bar
